<item>
  <title>Can a common blood thinner stop osteoarthritis?</title>
  <link>https://medicine.yale.edu/ortho/news-article/can-a-common-blood-thinner-stop-osteoarthritis-yale-study-reveals-dual-targeting-mechanism/</link>
  <description>Researchers at Yale School of Medicine discovered that dabigatran, an oral medication prescribed to prevent blood clots and reduce stroke risk, can dramatically suppress joint inflammation, protect cartilage, and restore joint function in animal models. The findings could lead to effective osteoarthritis&nbsp;therapies.</description>
  <author>news@yale.edu (Yale News)</author>

  <title>Yale program helps fathers reduce violence and strengthen families</title>
  <link>https://medicine.yale.edu/childstudy/news-article/fathers-for-change-strengthens-families/</link>
  <description>Can fathers with a history of violence change? Yale research and practice say yes. Yale Child Study Center’s Fathers for Change program helps reduce intimate partner violence, strengthen parenting, and support healthier family&nbsp;relationships.</description>

  <title>International collaborators share particle physics research at Yale</title>
  <link>https://wlab.yale.edu/posts/2026-10-30-relativistic-heavy-ion-group-hosts-international-collaborators-at-wright-lab</link>
  <description>Members of the Faculty of Nuclear Sciences and Physical Engineering at Czech Technical University in Prague who work on the STAR experiment at the Department of Energy’s Brookhaven National Laboratory in Long Island, New York, recently visited Wright Lab’s Relativistic Heavy Ion Group to share their&nbsp;research.</description>

<item>
  <title>‘Home’ for the holiday: A campus tradition offers Yalies far from home a seat at the Thanksgiving table </title>
  <link>https://news.yale.edu/2026/11/24/home-holiday-campus-tradition-offers-yalies-far-home-seat-thanksgiving-table</link>
  <description>Since 2001, members of the Yale community have opened their homes to international students and scholars through the “Thanksgiving at Home” program, offering their guests a taste of the uniquely American tradition — and creating new&nbsp;friendships.</description>

  <link>https://www.yalemedicine.org/news/actinic-keratosis-a-common-skin-condition-thats-worth-treating</link>
  <description>Worried about a rough spot on your skin? Yale Medicine dermatologists Sean R. Christensen and Kathleen C. Suozzi explain what actinic keratosis looks and feels like, who is most likely to develop it, and why treatment&nbsp;matters.</description>

<item>
  <title>Can AI drive a hard bargain?</title>
  <link>https://cowles.yale.edu/news/261119/can-ai-drive-hard-bargain</link>
  <description>In 15,000 simulated negotiations, Yale researchers find that the best AI negotiators open high, give ground strategically and still close nearly every deal, while “agreeable” models leave money on the&nbsp;table.</description>
  <author>news@yale.edu (Yale News)</author>

  <title>GLP-1s and the biology of obesity</title>
  <link>https://news.yale.edu/2026/11/24/glp-1s-and-biology-obesity</link>
  <description>In this episode of Beyond Blue, Yale endocrinologist Ania Jastreboff discusses the science of obesity, biology’s role, and how new research is opening the door to better treatment.
